title: Large Projects
concept: Managing large XIOM projects with workspaces — structuring code across multiple packages, sharing dependencies, and coordinating builds.
why: As projects grow beyond 10K lines, a single package becomes unwieldy. Workspaces split code into focused packages with shared dependencies and coordinated builds.
theory:
## Multi-Package Projects

### Workspace Structure

```
myproject/
├── package.xi          # Workspace root
├── packages/
│   ├── core/           # Core library
│   │   └── package.xi
│   ├── api/            # API server
│   │   └── package.xi
│   ├── cli/            # CLI tool
│   │   └── package.xi
│   └── shared/         # Shared types
│       └── package.xi
└── target/             # Shared build output
```

### Root package.xi (Workspace)

```xiom
workspace myproject
  members [
    "packages/core",
    "packages/api",
    "packages/cli",
    "packages/shared",
  ]
```

### Package Dependencies

```xiom
// packages/api/package.xi
package api
  version "0.1.0"

  deps [
    { name: "core", path: "../core" },
    { name: "shared", path: "../shared" },
    { name: "xiom.http", version: "^0.3.0" },
  ]
```

### Workspace Commands

```sh
# Build all packages
xiom build --workspace

# Build specific package
xiom build -p api

# Test all packages
xiom test --workspace

# Run a specific binary
xiom run -p cli -- --help
```

### Shared Dependency Resolution

Workspaces share a lockfile and dependency cache. All packages use the same version of shared dependencies, avoiding version conflicts.

### Build Coordination

```
shared (no deps)          → built first
core (depends: shared)    → built second
api (depends: core)       → built third
cli (depends: core)       → built in parallel with api!
```

### Best Practices for Large Projects

1. **Small packages**: Each package does ONE thing well
2. **Clear dependency direction**: core → api, not api → core → api
3. **Shared build output**: One target/ directory, faster incremental builds
4. **Consistent versioning**: All packages versioned together for releases
5. **Test isolation**: Each package has its own tests, easily run independently
syntax_ref:
// workspace.xi:
workspace name
  members ["pkg1", "pkg2", ...]

// Commands:
xiom build --workspace      # Build all
xiom test -p package_name   # Test one
xiom run -p package_name    # Run one binary
tips: Workspaces are the default for any project with 2+ packages — even small ones
Shared build output means faster incremental builds across the whole workspace
Keep packages small and focused — a package with 100 files should be split
Workspace-level commands (build --workspace, test --workspace) save time in CI
common_mistakes: Circular dependencies: api depends on core, core depends on api
Putting everything in one package because 'workspaces are complex' — one 1000-file package is more complex
Not sharing the lockfile — leads to version mismatches between packages
